correctness.rationale: The defining recursion yields aligned triples (a_m,1-a_m,a_m). Equal neighboring bits can begin only at residue 2 mod 3. Of four consecutive a_m=x_(2m), one adjacent pair is x_(3j), x_(3j+2), hence equal; therefore there is no 10-bit alternating run. In a period-p cube with gcd(p,3)=1, an equal pair would recur at starting positions with different residues modulo 3 (two positions even in the seam case), impossible. Thus the entire cube alternates. Its period is even, and 3p<=9 yields p=2. The example 101010101 at indices 12..20 proves sharp exponent 9/2, and any period-p factor shorter than a cube has exponent<3. The exact standalone recurrence and digit-parity program tested all eligible periods <=120 over a 50,000-symbol prefix; the proof, not the finite test, is universal.

originality.rationale: The 2023 source poses the general critical-exponent question and proves only the generating recurrence; a related study gives an alternating fourth power but not an upper bound. The later 2026 factor/frequency paper and exact OEIS table do not state or imply the all-period coprime-to-three cube classification or the sharp exponent 9/2. Search across aliases and equivalent formulations found no covering statement. The proof introduces an obstruction from adjacent equalities at mod-three block boundaries. Unindexed equivalent results remain possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed literature on the same rational-base sequence could independently contain an equivalent cube classification.

value.rationale: The 2023 source explicitly asks for the critical exponent of this rational-base word. The proved statement resolves the sharp exponent for the canonical mod-three period sector forced by its two-to-three block substitution and classifies every cubic factor in that sector, excluding infinitely many potential high-exponent periods. It is a structural obstruction and exact natural partial spectrum rather than an arbitrary cutoff, though the global conjecture remains open.
